- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Ports #8334 to dev. That PR re-architected the internals of CheckpointWithoutOutput in megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py. This PR also moves dev's mHC recompute features onto the new internals. No public API or call site changes.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

Preserve all parameter types, defaults, and constructor bodies. Acceptance (proposed static check): all three newly introduced constructors declare `-> None`, with their initialization logic unchanged.

Strict review passed, with no significant issues found. LGTM.

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 0

**Follow-up scope.** This review checks the one finding from the last bot review (head `d4bb27a`) and the changes made since then. I read the code; I did not run any tests.

**Prior finding, now fixed.** The last review asked for the style guide's `-> None` return type on the three new constructors. All three now have it:
- `_ArgLayout.__init__` at [random.py#L921](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L921)
- `_TERecomputeContext.__init__` at [random.py#L947](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L947)
- `_RecomputeRegion.__init__` at [random.py#L1025-L1032](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L1025-L1032)

The parameter types, defaults and constructor bodies are unchanged.

**What changed since the last review.**
- In [random.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py), I compared the old and new versions of everything the PR changes. That covers `_RegionState` through `CheckpointWithoutOutput.discard_output_and_register_recompute`, plus `MHCCheckpointManager` and `CheckpointWithoutOutputManager`. The only differences are the three annotations above.
- Both test files are byte-identical to the last reviewed version: [test_random.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py) and [test_hybrid_block.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_hybrid_block.py).
- The module uses `from __future__ import annotations`, so the new return annotations have no runtime effect. They cannot change the region's lifecycle, RNG replay, the FP8/TE context or how released storage is shared.

**Risk.** Low. This update only adds annotations. Nothing in it needs reporting under this follow-up's rules, and no earlier finding is still open.

+class _ArgLayout:
+    """Positional layout of a call: tensors travel through autograd, other values stay here."""
+
+    def __init__(self, args: tuple) -> None:

+    Saving through ``save_for_backward`` keeps the inputs visible to active
+    ``saved_tensors_hooks`` (e.g. fine-grained activation offloading) and to the CUDA graph
+    saved-tensor observer, like inputs saved by any other op. The returned token never takes
+    part in a loss, so ``backward`` never runs; the inputs are read back once, through
+    ``token.grad_fn.saved_tensors``, when the region is rebuilt. As for any custom Function, the

+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, *grads):
+        """Never called: the token is not used by any loss."""
+        raise RuntimeError("The input stash of CheckpointWithoutOutput must not reach a loss.")
+
+
+class _RegionFunction(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Autograd node that stands in for the checkpointed function.
+
+    It keeps its region in ``ctx.region`` so that backward can route the output gradients through
+    the recomputed graph.
     """
 
     @staticmethod
-    def forward(
-        ctx: Any,
-        run_function: Callable[[Unpack[_Ts]], _R],
-        checkpoint_without_output_obj: CheckpointWithoutOutput,
-        *args: Unpack[_Ts],
-    ) -> _R:
-        """Forward pass."""
-        if checkpoint_without_output_obj.fp8:
-            fp8 = FP8GlobalStateManager.is_fp8_enabled()
-            ctx.fp8 = fp8
-            ctx.fp8_recipe = FP8GlobalStateManager.get_fp8_recipe() if fp8 else None
-            fwd_ctx = activation_recompute_forward(activation_recompute=True, recompute_phase=False)
+    def forward(ctx, region, *tensors):
+        """Run the function once without recording a graph."""
+        ctx.region = region
+        return region.run_without_graph(tensors)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, *grad_outputs):
+        """Back-propagate through the rebuilt graph and return the input gradients."""
+        region, ctx.region = ctx.region, None
+        if region is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "CheckpointWithoutOutput does not support running backward through the same "
+                "graph twice."
+            )
+        return (None,) + region.backpropagate(grad_outputs)
+
+
+class _RecomputeRegion:
+    """One call of a checkpointed function, plus what is needed to re-run it in backward.
+
+    The region keeps ``detach()``-ed aliases of the outputs rather than the outputs themselves:
+    an output reaches ``_RegionFunction`` through its grad_fn, and that node owns the region, so
+    holding the output would close a reference cycle through the autograd graph.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        function: Callable,
+        args: tuple,
+        use_te_context: bool,
+        retain_input_tensors: bool,
+        output_slot: Optional[Any] = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.state: Optional[_RegionState] = None
+        self._function = function
+        self._layout = _ArgLayout(args)
+        # Taken before the function draws any random number. The snapshot is per checkpoint,
+        # not per recompute group, and has to stay that way: each checkpoint's recompute must
+        # rewind to the offsets its own forward saw. Sharing one group-level snapshot would
+        # rewind every member to the first checkpoint's state, so any RNG the group consumed
+        # in between would replay the wrong draw. The cost is one clone_state() per tracked
+        # state per checkpoint.
+        self._rng_states = _get_all_rng_states()
+        self._te_context = _TERecomputeContext(use_te_context)
+        self._retained_storage_ptrs = (
+            frozenset(t.untyped_storage().data_ptr() for t in self._layout.tensors_of(args))
+            if retain_input_tensors
+            else frozenset()
+        )
+        # Optional MHCRecomputeArenaSlot that the function writes its single output into.
+        self._output_slot = output_slot
+        self._stash: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+        self._output_aliases: tuple = ()
+        # (rebuilt outputs, rebuilt input leaves), kept from the rebuild until backward.
+        self._rebuilt: Optional[tuple] = None

+def test_checkpoint_without_output_multiple_hook_tensors():
+    """Discarding with several hook tensors on parallel consumers recomputes only once."""
+    grad_enabled_per_call = []
+
+    def gelu(x):
+        grad_enabled_per_call.append(torch.is_grad_enabled())
+        return torch.nn.functional.gelu(x)
+
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel()
+    try:
+        input1 = torch.randn(6, 8, requires_grad=True)
+        weight_a1 = torch.randn(8, 8, requires_grad=True)
+        weight_b1 = torch.randn(8, 8, requires_grad=True)
+        input2, weight_a2, weight_b2 = (
+            t.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True) for t in (input1, weight_a1, weight_b1)
+        )
+
+        checkpoint = CheckpointWithoutOutput()
+        hidden = checkpoint.checkpoint(gelu, input1)
+        out_a, out_b = hidden @ weight_a1, hidden @ weight_b1
+        checkpoint.discard_output_and_register_recompute(out_a)
+        checkpoint.discard_output_and_register_recompute(out_b)
+        (out_a.sum() + 2 * out_b.sum()).backward()
+        assert grad_enabled_per_call == [False, True]
+
+        hidden_ref = torch.nn.functional.gelu(input2)
+        ((hidden_ref @ weight_a2).sum() + 2 * (hidden_ref @ weight_b2).sum()).backward()
+        assert torch.allclose(input1.grad, input2.grad)
+        assert torch.allclose(weight_a1.grad, weight_a2.grad)
+        assert torch.allclose(weight_b1.grad, weight_b2.grad)
+    finally:
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()

- `_ArgLayout.__init__` at [random.py#L921](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L921)

The parameter types, defaults and constructor bodies are unchanged.

**What changed since the last review.**
- In [random.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py), I compared the old and new versions of everything the PR changes. That covers `_RegionState` through `CheckpointWithoutOutput.discard_output_and_register_recompute`, plus `MHCCheckpointManager` and `CheckpointWithoutOutputManager`. The only differences are the three annotations above.
- Both test files are byte-identical to the last reviewed version: [test_random.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py) and [test_hybrid_block.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7ad9ec3641c85d5e39b16111c00a8e1b2737ff54/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_hybrid_block.py).
